author: groganz-bot[bot]
body:
## Problem

The reusable `release-notes` job (`reusable-release-notes.yml`) fails its **"Verify tag is annotated + compute previous semver tag"** step with a **false** `FAIL: '<tag>' is a LIGHTWEIGHT tag` for tags that are genuinely annotated.

Observed in `cinatra-ai/drupal-module` on the ratified `v0.1.5` release tag: `v0.1.5` is a proper annotated tag object on the remote (`refs/tags/v0.1.5^{}` deref present; GitHub git-ref object type `tag`), yet the job failed as if it were lightweight.

## Root cause

The checkout step used `fetch-depth: 0` **without `fetch-tags: true`**. The runner log shows `actions/checkout`, after its initial `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` fetch, runs a **second fetch by commit SHA** into the tag ref:

```
git fetch --no-tags ... origin +43bd986…:refs/tags/v0.1.5
git checkout --force refs/tags/v0.1.5
```

That SHA-refspec fetch **overwrites the local `refs/tags/v0.1.5`** to point directly at the commit — a **lightweight** ref — clobbering the annotated tag object. The gate's `git cat-file -t "$TAG"` then returns `commit` instead of `tag`, tripping the lightweight-tag branch.

Reproduced locally: after the full tag fetch `cat-file -t = tag`; after the SHA-refspec fetch `= commit`; after re-fetching `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` `= tag` again. (`drupalorg-publish.yml` does **not** hit this because it already sets `fetch-tags: true`.)

## Fix (CI-determinism only — the annotated-tag contract is unchanged)

1. Add `fetch-tags: true` to the checkout step so the `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` refspec that carries the tag object survives.
2. Force-refetch tag refs in the `tagmeta` step immediately before the `cat-file` check — belt-and-suspenders against `actions/checkout`-version drift in that behaviour.

A **truly lightweight** remote tag still resolves to a `commit` after the force-fetch, so the gate still rejects real lightweight tags — the org release contract is preserved, not weakened. No product/runtime change.

## Risk / review

This edits `.github/workflows/**` → **HIGH-RISK**. Bot-authored (author ≠ approver) so it needs a fresh @groganz `APPROVED` review (the human verification arm). No secrets are touched.

## Downstream

`cinatra-ai/drupal-module` SHA-pins this reusable workflow (`github-release.yml @05a7dd58…`). A companion PR there bumps the pin to this fix's merge SHA; the drupal-module GitHub-Release decoration stays broken until BOTH this PR merges AND the pin-bump merges + the `v0.1.5` tag re-runs. The drupal.org publish (separate `drupalorg-publish.yml`) is unaffected and already correctly paused on the `release-approval` Environment.

author: kimerran
body:
Part of #18 (item 1 — lifecycle auto-lock). Does **not** close #18; the other security items (biometric unlock, dependency vuln, release signing) are tracked separately (see the triage comment on #18).

## Problem
The wallet only auto-locked via the idle timer (`armAutoLock` in `core/session/handler.ts`). Backgrounding the app (home button / app switcher) left the decrypted session in memory for the full idle window, even though the OS may keep the process alive — so the wallet could sit unlocked behind the lock screen.

## Change
- Added `@capacitor/app` and a native-only `pause` listener in `useWallet` that locks immediately when the app is backgrounded (reusing the existing `LOCK` path, so the session is cleared and the UI shows Unlock on resume).
- The listener is gated on `isNativePlatform()` and dynamically imported, so the **extension build is unaffected** (same pattern as the status-bar plugin). The idle timer remains as a fallback.
- Registered the plugin in the native project via `npx cap update android` (`capacitor.settings.gradle`, `capacitor.build.gradle`).

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (63/63), and `npm run build:mobile` all pass; confirmed the `pause`/`addListener` wiring is present in the mobile bundle.
- ⚠️ Not exercised on a device/emulator in the agent environment — the actual background→lock→resume behavior should be smoke-tested on the built APK.

## Design note
Locks **immediately** on background (secure default, matches the issue). A short grace period for quick app-switching could be layered on later if desired.

## Summary

A 49-agent workflow (7 module-group analyzers + one adversarial verifier per finding) audited the whole codebase; **41/42 findings survived** adversarial review. Everything offline-measurable was shipped with regression tests, then a `python-reviewer` pass caught 3 follow-ups (2 fixed, 2 Low accepted/documented).

- **Suite 640 → 722 passed** (+82; every fix carries ≥1 regression test)
- **ruff clean**, coverage total **94% held** (touched modules ≥ baseline: cache 100%, render 97%, pdf 95%, mapsite 97%)
- Root-caused, conservative, reversible; SSRF/trust-boundary untouched (verified by reviewer)

## Correctness fixes
- **Cache**: missing/corrupt blob self-heals to a miss (was: raised into every cached tool for the TTL); `key()` no longer lowercases path/query (RFC 3986 — `/API` vs `/api` served wrong content)
- **Throttle**: per-host courtesy delay held under concurrency (batch_read's 8 same-host requests burst simultaneously; now slot-reserved)
- **Render**: challenge pages (`success=True` "Just a moment…") raise `blocked_by_antibot` instead of becoming article content; wedged Chromium bounded by `asyncio.timeout` (was: permanent permit starvation)
- **Rerank**: safety-floor backfills around relevant hits instead of replacing them with junk; URL dedup keeps meaningful query params (`?v=AAA` vs `?v=BBB`); relevance guard ignores stopword-only overlap
- **Router**: modal "may" no longer misroutes to news
- **research**: per-source isolation restored (one bad source killed the whole bundle)
- **PDF**: pages-spec validation (`schema_invalid` not `not_pdf`); spec-legal leading junk accepted; quality tier honors `pages`
- **map_urls**: gzipped `.xml.gz` sitemaps decompressed (were silent mojibake); **article extractor**: only adjacent duplicate blocks collapse
- **Trading**: ForexFactory non-dict/impact-passthrough/`date_range` validation; **watch** honors `interval_s` on error + persist rollback/isolation; **crawl** real deadline + clamps + semaphore + coded errors; **cot** date filter + live drift detectors + coded errors

## Added
Cache eviction (bounded VPS disk); 4 tools cached (read_pdf/ff/cot/news); degraded results never cached; `argus_tool_errors_total` metrics; smart_search specialist failover; github `incomplete_results` signal; news degraded propagation.

## Changed
Article metadata extraction ~4x cheaper (`extract_metadata` vs `bare_extraction`, measured 1.50→0.38 ms/call). Docs refreshed (TOOL-SPECS, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG 0.4.0).

## Deferred (explicitly)
`_SEM_FLOOR` recalibration + semantic-rescue guard alignment — change rerank scores, gated on the live semantic A/B harness (needs SearXNG + LLM judge), not shippable on unit tests alone.

Fixes OPE-208 by closing the admin create-user custom-data validation gap for snake_case reserved/generated user fields.

## Root Cause

### Routes (all in `backend/src/routes/boards.js`, mounted at `/api/boards`)

| Method | Path | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| POST | `/api/boards` | `requireFields(title, category, imageUrl)`; validates category against enum; returns 201 + full body |
| GET | `/api/boards/:id` | `include: { cards: true }`; `HttpError(404)` when null |
| DELETE | `/api/boards/:id` | Cascades to Card via FK; relies on Prisma P2025 -> central errorHandler for 404 |
| GET | `/api/boards` | Optional `category`, `filter=recent`, `search`; incremental where-clause builder |

Each route uses one of the three shape-setting idioms Enes should imitate:
- `POST /api/boards` -> validate + create + 201-with-full-body (for his `POST /api/boards/:boardId/cards`)
- `GET /api/boards/:id` -> findUnique + 404-if-null (for his two PATCH routes)
- `DELETE /api/boards/:id` -> delete + 204 + P2025-goes-to-errorHandler (for his `DELETE /api/cards/:id`)

### Contract diffs (per `frontend-planning.md` Section 5.6)

- **`Board.imageUrl` is now required.** Schema: `String?` -> `String`. `requireFields` includes `imageUrl`. planning.md Sections 2 and 3 updated.
- **`Card.title` added as a required field.** Schema gets a new `title String` column. planning.md Sections 1 (CardTile, CreateCardModal), 2 (POST /cards request + response), 3 (Card table), and 4 (CreateCardModal state table) updated. Enes wires validation into `POST /api/boards/:boardId/cards` when he starts on cards.js.

Migration file: `backend/prisma/migrations/20260701233711_require_image_url_and_add_card_title/`.

### Prisma 7 runtime fix

The runtime PrismaClient no longer accepts `datasourceUrl` or `datasources` options and requires a driver adapter (per the Prisma 7 upgrade guide). `prisma.config.ts` remains the source of truth for the CLI, but the runtime client now uses `@prisma/adapter-pg` reading `DATABASE_URL` from `process.env`. `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `pg` added as runtime deps.

Without this fix, any query would throw `PrismaClient needs to be constructed with non-empty valid PrismaClientOptions`.

author: fadhlanr
body:
## What & why

The mini card chooser rendered every result row with each card's own `fitted` template, so custom subclass templates leaked into the list. Rows should render uniformly regardless of card type.

The index already prerenders `fitted` across the full ancestor chain (one entry per render type, CardDef included), so the chooser pins its rows with `htmlQuery: { eq: { format: 'fitted', renderType: CardDef } }` — a host-only query binding. No prerender-pipeline, index-schema, or migration changes.

## Why not ancestor-aware atom (the ticket's initial direction)

The ticket was scoped on the assumption that the mini chooser rows render in the **atom** format, so the plan was to make atom ancestor-aware in the index — per-ancestor `atom_html` JSONB map, a migration that wipes `boxel_index` (full reindex of every realm on deploy), and one extra atom render per ancestor per card at indexing time — and then query `atom + renderType: CardDef`.

In fact the chooser already renders its rows in the **fitted** format; the uniformity problem was only that each row used the card's *own* fitted template. Since fitted is already prerendered per ancestor, pinning the existing fitted rendering to the CardDef render type solves the actual problem with a query binding alone. The ancestor-aware-atom index change would have added indexing cost and a disruptive migration to serve a format the chooser doesn't use.

## Changes

- `panel-content.gts` — for `variant === 'mini'`, `withMiniHtmlQuery` injects the fitted + CardDef htmlQuery into both the main-search and recents wire queries through the wire filter's top-level `eq`; the search-entry engine lifts the binding out and dissolves the now-empty `eq`, leaving the rest of the filter untouched. Non-mini variants keep the native fitted default.
- The URL-paste / live-recents fallback tiles already render through `CardRenderer` with `@codeRef` pointing at CardDef, so they match the prerendered rows without changes.

## Tests

- New `mini-card-chooser-test` case: a card that overrides its own `fitted` template renders the CardDef default fitted tile (`.fitted-template`) in its row — not its custom template — and selection still fires onSelect with the canonical URL.
- Ancestor-level `renderType` matching in the engine is covered by the existing search-entries-engine test ("a renderType predicate renders a subclass as its ancestor").

author: reubenmiller
body:
## Summary

Fixes two usability traps that surfaced while writing the tedge-dot Cloud Fieldbus e2e suite:

1. **Operation assertion keywords now accept an operation id or an `AssertOperation`.** Previously, passing an id (e.g. captured from a REST response or another suite variable) failed with `'str' object has no attribute 'assert_success'`. All eight `Operation Should …` keywords now coerce ids by fetching the operation.

2. **New keyword `Execute Shell Command And Get Output`.** `Execute Shell Command` is asynchronous and returns the operation — but the name invites using the return value as text, and e.g. `Should Contain    ${output}    something` then fails with the opaque `TypeError: argument of type 'AssertOperation' is not a container or iterable`. The new keyword waits for the operation to be SUCCESSFUL and returns the `c8y_Command.result` string:

   ```robotframework
   ${output}=    Execute Shell Command And Get Output    cat /etc/os-release    timeout=60
   Should Contain    ${output}    debian
   ```

   The existing keyword keeps its behaviour; its docstring now points to the new one.

Both paths are exercised with mocked-client smoke tests through the real retry stack (id coercion → assert_success, and output extraction).

## Summary

Adds \`POST /api/translate\` — a daemon-side bridge to Google's free (unofficial) gtx translate endpoint. Powers the **select-to-lookup** feature landing in onebrain-webui 0.1.7 (paired PR in \`onebrain-ai/onebrain-webui\`): the browser POSTs selected text, the daemon calls the provider and returns \`{translated, detected_from, truncated}\`.

## Design points

- **Bundled preflight fix (found during live QA):** redirect `Location` resolution now handles scheme-relative (`//host/…`) and absolute-path forms per RFC 3986 — th.wikipedia Special:Search redirects were wrongly reported unframeable; SSRF posture unchanged.

- **Fixed host** (\`translate.googleapis.com\`) — no user-controlled URL, no SSRF surface; auth via the existing \`/api\` token middleware
- **Bounded both ways**: 5,000-char request cap (Unicode-safe \`chars()\` truncation + \`truncated\` flag) · 8 s outbound timeout · ureq's built-in 10 MB response cap
- **Complete status mapping**: 400 (empty text / bad lang code, validated pre-network) · 502 (provider unreachable / unparseable) · 500 (blocking-task failure)
- Same \`spawn_blocking\` + ureq idiom as the webview preflight; lang codes allowlisted \`[A-Za-z0-9-]{2,8}\`
- Provider is a single-function swap point for future DeepL/LibreTranslate options

- Unit: gtx URL encoding, response parsing (real captured shape incl. Thai), garbage rejection, lang-code allowlist, handler validation (400s)

3-round whole-branch review (correctness/integration → adversarial security/consistency → fresh-eyes maintainer + regression sweep): all READY. One doc finding (route-table row) fixed in-branch.

body:
### Summary

Replaces the synchronous crash-and-restart step-down (wts_reopen()) in disagg_switch_roles() with an async step-down that keeps worker threads live during the role transition, exercising concurrent reads and writes against the actual leader-to-follower handoff.

Async step-down is now enabled by setting g.disagg_stepdown_async = true before calling operations(). The old disagg.step_down config knob has been removed.

Async step-down sequence (disagg_async_stepdown())

- Stop checkpoint and timestamp threads — prevents interference while establishing the step-down boundary.
- Freeze timestamp allocation — take the write lock on timestamp_lock, capture step_down_ts = g.timestamp, advance g.timestamp += 2, then release the lock. Threads waiting on the lock unblock with freshly allocated timestamps > step_down_ts and route to ingest.
- Notify WT via set_timestamp(step_down_timestamp=step_down_ts) — in-flight write transactions with commit_ts <= step_down_ts are rolled back.
- Drain — poll all_durable >= step_down_ts every 250 ms with a 60 s timeout. all_durable guarantees no commit gaps remain below the boundary.
- Pin stable at step_down_ts via set_timestamp(stable=step_down_ts) — this happens only after the drain confirms all transactions at or below the boundary have committed or rolled back.
- Step-down checkpoint — assert stable == step_down_ts .
- Become follower via reconfigure(role=follower) — workers remain live for the follower window, exercising reads and ingest writes.
- Handoff cleanup — follower_read_latest_checkpoint(), wts_prepare_discover(), reset flags.

alloc_timestamp(session) now holds the timestamp_lock read lock around every g.timestamp++, covering commit, rollback-for-prepared, and prepare timestamps. The lock is uncontended in steady state and excluded only during the notification. Once the arm's write lock releases, every newly allocated timestamp is strictly greater than step_down_ts.

## Summary

ms-98 五部作の最終ピース。 \`_claim_operation_fire_for_bus_push\` の fail-open policy を狭め、 **429 / circuit-open は skip、 他 exception は既存 fail-open** の分岐にする。 07-02 の positive feedback loop を client 側から完全に絶つ。

## 背景と根拠

SPEC §設計方針 1 の fail-open policy は「network 一時故障で silent lost fire を防ぐ」ため。 だが 07-02 では:
- Cloud Run 429 → \`RuntimeError\` → 既存 fail-open で return True → bus event push 強行
- 並列 bclaude 全 session が同じ挙動 → server にさらに負荷 → 429 rate 悪化
- **fail-open が storm の amplifier として機能** していた

- exception message に \`"429"\` or \`"circuit open"\` が含まれる → return False (= skip this tick、 stderr に \"rate-limited; will retry next tick\" log)
- その他 exception (ConnectionError / AttributeError / missing creds 等) → 既存 fail-open (return True) 継続

- server 過負荷時: 発火強行が消える → storm 収束が早まる
- 通常不具合: 従来通り fail-open で silent lost fire を防ぐ

author: critaswang
body:
## Summary

Fixes two defects in the Data Preview of table-model TsFiles, plus a related `atob` regression.

### 1. Header/body column misalignment
On table-model files, `measurements` also contains the tag columns (e.g. `plant`, `device`). The fixed **device** column used `key`/`dataIndex = "device"`, colliding with a tag column also named `device`. Since antdv `Table` distinguishes columns by `key`, the header desynced from the body, and `flatRow.device` was overwritten by the measurement value.

**Fix**: the fixed identity column now uses a reserved key `__device__`, fully isolated from tag columns. Tree-model files are unaffected.

### 2. Timestamps rendered as `NaN-NaN-NaN NaN:NaN:NaN.NaN`
Source timestamps can be nanoseconds (19 digits, e.g. `1692611833503000000`), which overflow JS `Date` → `Invalid Date` → `NaN`.

**Fix**:
- Added `normalizeToMs()` (in `utils/timestamp.ts`) to auto-scale seconds / milliseconds / microseconds / nanoseconds to milliseconds.
- Display stays at millisecond precision. The **exact** original value is preserved without a backend change via a scoped `transformResponse` hook that captures the raw timestamp digit string **before** `JSON.parse` (avoiding lossy `double` conversion), exposed on hover, with an info banner explaining the behavior.
- CSV export timestamps now use `normalizeToMs` too.

### 3. `atob` regression fix
After fileIds became URL-safe base64, `atob()` failed on `-`/`_` characters (and never handled UTF-8 for non-ASCII paths). Extracted `encodeFileId`/`decodeFileId` into `utils/fileId.ts` and replaced all six call sites (file tree, data-preview, chart, metadata).

## Testing
- `pnpm build` (vue-tsc + vite) passes.
- Verified end-to-end in the browser on a real nanosecond table-model file: columns align, timestamp displays as `2023-08-21 17:57:13.503`, hover shows the exact raw value, and sub-millisecond precision is preserved losslessly (raw string `...123456` kept exact, vs `...123500` under naive `String(double)`).

## Notes
`timestampRaw` is currently preserved only on the data-preview endpoint. The chart endpoint could get the same treatment if full nanosecond fidelity is needed there.

## Description

Add three features to improve LiteLLM for Chinese developers:

1. **Task-Aware Routing Strategy** - Routes requests based on task type
2. **China Domestic Free Sources** - Pre-configured free sources for Chinese developers
3. **Local-First Routing Strategy** - Prioritizes local models for latency/cost

## Motivation

Chinese developers face unique challenges:
- Need VPN to access international LLM APIs
- Prefer local models for latency and privacy
- Different model preferences for different tasks

This PR addresses all three issues with a complete solution.

## Changes

### 1. Task-Aware Routing Strategy
- New `TaskAwareRoutingStrategy` class in `router_strategy/task_aware_routing.py`
- Routes requests based on task type (coding, chinese, general, english, fast)
- Users can define task-specific model preferences

### 2. China Domestic Free Sources Configuration
- Example config in `proxy/example_config_yaml/china_domestic_free_sources.yaml`
- Pre-configured SiliconFlow and Zhipu models
- Accessible from mainland China without VPN

### 3. Local-First Routing Strategy
- New `LocalFirstRoutingStrategy` class in `router_strategy/local_first_routing.py`
- Routes to local models first (e.g., Ollama)
- Falls back to cloud models when local unavailable

### 4. Documentation

- `docs/my-website/docs/routing/local-first-routing.md`
- `docs/my-website/docs/routing/china-domestic-free-sources.md`

router_settings:

router_settings:

Rewrote `WeaponViewmodels` from a primitive builder into a GLB loader:
- Each gun carries its own arms + skeleton and plays **draw** (on equip) → looping **idle**, plus **fire** (on shoot) and **reload** (on R) via `AnimationMixer`.

20 commits of canvas/strip UI work (~+460/−130 across `EqCurveDisplay`, `BandEditStrip`, `PluginEditor`).

## Floating edit-strip placement (the branch's namesake)
Placement of the selected-band strip is now a pluggable strategy (View menu, persisted), 5 modes:
- **Classic** — centered above/below the node (the original)
- **Anchor-side** — extends into the open side
- **Collision-aware** — avoids nodes, draws a node↔strip leader line
- **Hybrid** — floats, docks to an edge when the graph is crowded
- **Fixed-lane** — permanent bottom lane, FabFilter-style

## Vertical dB scale
±3/6/12/30 dB combo (top-right, persisted) + drag auto-zoom: dragging a node past the visible edge steps the scale out (rate-limited), with the gain-drag anchor re-based on each step so the node never jumps.

## Add-band ("+") rework
Click places the node exactly at the cursor; HP/LP/Notch land on the 0 dB line; Notch zone = the bottom strip of the plot; boost/cut amount scales with the visible dB range; placement capped at 20 kHz. One source of truth (`predictAdd`) drives both the action and the ghost preview.

## Honest curves at the edges
- Curves are **designed at an oversampled rate (≥96k)**, not the session fs — LP/BP dive smoothly off the right edge at any sample rate instead of flattening + kinking near Nyquist (analog intent, Pro-Q-style). The analyzer still uses the real fs (measured content).
- Curves dive off the window bottom instead of piling on the floor line; stable notch tips (curve sampled at every band's f0 + floor clamp).
- The 20–28k display-only region dissolves into fog past Nyquist; bottom freq-axis strip is reserved so labels are never painted over; ghost preview clipped to the plot like everything else.

## Notch + strip polish
- Notch width edits in octaves everywhere (whiskers, wheel, edit strip).
- Fixed strip width with a permanently reserved [M][S] slot (right of ST); `< index >` nav always visible — the strip never resizes on ST↔M/S toggle.

Verified: builds VST3/AU/Standalone/CLAP; standalone launched and exercised (selection, strip re-anchoring, scale combo, LP dive) on this branch as rebased onto the v0.1.5 fcore pin.

author: lawrencecchen
body:
## Summary

iOS optimistic scroll (https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/6067) had three unreconciled viewport owners: the phone's UIScrollView delta stream, the phone's local Ghostty mirror, and the Mac's real viewport (which the scroll RPC also moved). Render-grid exports follow the Mac's live `vp_top` (`ghostty/src/apprt/embedded.zig`), so every phone gesture was applied twice: the mirror scrolled locally over stale prefetched history while the Mac's scrolled viewport repainted the mirror's hidden screen rows, and the two offsets drifted apart on clamping and coalescing. On top of that, scrollback prefetch responses arrive as full `ESC c` snapshots that reset the mirror and snapped the viewport to the bottom mid-drag.

This makes the phone the single owner of the primary-screen viewport and the Mac the single owner of content:

- `TerminalScrollRouting` (new, pure): primary-screen gestures send NO scroll delta to the Mac; the RPC is only used to fetch history windows (`delta_lines=0`, already a no-op scroll on the Mac, so old hosts are compatible). Alternate screen still forwards wheel deltas to the real PTY for TUIs.
- Full render-grid replays now go through `GhosttySurfaceView.processFullReplacementOutputAndWait`, which captures the mirror's scrollback offset-from-bottom before the `ESC c` rebuild and re-applies it after via the row-exact `scroll_page_lines` binding action (the wheel path is subject to the 3x discrete `mouse-scroll-multiplier` and would overshoot). Invariant: an authoritative content rebuild never moves the phone-owned viewport. At the bottom (cold attach) it is a no-op.
- Sustained scrolling into history pages the prefetch window deeper (600 rows per refresh); the Mac-side prefetch cap rises from 600 to 4800 rows.
- The mirror's Ghostty scrollbar geometry (`GHOSTTY_ACTION_SCROLLBAR`) plus a monotonic update counter are now recorded in all builds (was DEBUG-only) to drive the offset restore.

## Red/green (simulator-verified locally)

- Red `1455fe519d`: `CMUX_FULL_REPLAY_SCROLL_STRESS` harness + `cmuxUITests/testScrollbackPositionSurvivesAuthoritativeFullReplay`. The harness requires a post-replay scrollbar callback before judging, so the stale cached geometry cannot produce a false pass. Verified failing on iPhone 17 Pro sim: dock shows `scrollAtBottom=1`, `bottomStressPhase=regressed` (replay snapped the viewport to the bottom).
- Green `75acd90510`: offset capture/restore. Verified passing on the same sim.

## Testing

- `swift test --package-path Packages/iOS/CmuxMobileShell` passed (incl. new `TerminalScrollRouting` + prefetch paging tests)
- iOS sim compile checks: `CmuxMobileTerminal`, `CmuxMobileShellUI`, `ios/cmuxPackage` build for `arm64-apple-ios26.0-simulator`
- New XCUITest run locally red→green as above (`CMUX_ALLOW_LOCAL_TEST=1`, isolated derived data)

## Localization

No user-facing strings changed (debug harness phases and test identifiers only); no localization updates needed.

## Related

- https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/6067 (optimistic scroll feature)
- https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/7153 (bottom-scroll anchoring, scrollbar bridge this reuses)
- https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/issues/7160 (same family: viewport-relative repaints compositing rows)

body:
## Summary

* This is a…
  * [x] Bug fix
  * [ ] Feature addition
  * [x] Refactoring
  * [ ] Minor / simple change (like a typo)
  * [ ] Other
* **Describe this change in 1-2 sentences**: Replace `encode_filename()` with `resolve_fs_path()` — a new function that resolves file paths against the filesystem using Unicode NFC/NFD normalization fallback. This fixes the `MutagenError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory` when saving files with accented characters on byte-exact filesystems (macOS → SMB → Linux ext4).

## Problem

* JIRA ticket: PICARD-3331 (also related: PICARD-644, PICARD-2055)

On macOS, `encode_filename()` always converted file paths from Python `str` to `bytes` before passing them to Mutagen. When files reside on a byte-exact filesystem (e.g. SMB mount backed by Linux ext4), and the stored filename uses a different Unicode normalization (NFC vs NFD) than what the filesystem has, the bytes don't match and the file cannot be found.

Example: A file stored as NFD `Franc\xcc\xa7oise` (decomposed ç) on the server fails to open when Picard produces NFC bytes `Fran\xc3\xa7oise` (composed ç).

This also affects Linux where `os.path.supports_unicode_filenames` is `False`, causing `encode_filename` to return bytes there as well.

## Solution

1. **Add `resolve_fs_path(filename: str | bytes | Path) -> str`** — resolves a path against the filesystem, trying NFC and NFD normalization alternatives if the file isn't found. Zero overhead in the common case (file exists → immediate return).

2. **Call `resolve_fs_path` at external path entry points** — where paths come from Qt (drag & drop, file dialogs, URLs) or CLI arguments. Called once before `normpath`. Also called after file save/rename to ensure `self.filename` matches the on-disk representation.

3. **Remove `encode_filename()` from all format handlers** — Mutagen receives `str` paths directly, which the OS handles correctly on all platforms.

4. **Remove `encode_filename()` and `decode_filename()`** entirely — they have no remaining callers. The root cause of the bug (forcing bytes) is eliminated.

5. **Fix `_shorten_to_bytes_length`** — uses `os.fsencode()` / `os.fsdecode()` for byte-length calculation.

### Convention established

- `resolve_fs_path()` is called **once** when a path enters the pipeline from an external source (Qt dialogs, drag & drop, CLI). Not needed for paths from `os.scandir`/`os.listdir` or files we just created.
- All downstream code (format handlers, stat calls, cover art) receives an already-resolved `str`
- No more `str` → `bytes` → `str` round-trips for file I/O

## Summary

Posting no longer paints any background of its own — the entire UI is rendered on the bare terminal background, for every theme (built-in, user, and Xresources themes).

The earlier attempt in #4 set CSS backgrounds to `transparent`, but Textual still flattens those cells onto the theme's background color, so the real terminal background never showed through. This PR uses Textual's ANSI passthrough mechanism instead:

- **`themes.py`**: new `use_terminal_background()` forces every theme's `background` / `surface` / `panel` / `boost` to `ansi_default` (the terminal's own default color) and forces the background-related theme variables (footer, scrollbar, cursors, hover, links) to `transparent`. Applied to all built-in themes and to `Theme.to_textual_theme()`, which also covers user themes and Xresources themes. Derived shades (`surface-lighten-1`, `accent-muted`, …) resolve to `ansi_default` automatically.
- **`app.py`**: Textual's `ANSIToTruecolor` filter would convert `ansi_default` cells into opaque RGB approximations, so it is disabled at init and kept disabled across theme changes (Textual normally re-enables it for any theme other than `textual-ansi`).
- **CSS**: remaining explicit paints removed — modal / command palette / jump overlay dim layers (`black 25–33%`), button fills (`$primary` / `$accent`), key-value edit-mode fills, and the selected tree node now use `transparent`.
- **Cursors** indicate their position with reverse video instead of a painted background. Text selection backgrounds are intentionally kept, since a transparent selection would be invisible.
- **Docs**: theme guide notes that a theme's `background` / `surface` colors are now ignored.
- **Tests**: all snapshots regenerated for the transparent UI.

## Test plan

- Headless verification: rendered cells carry `bgcolor=default` (terminal default) and the truecolor filter stays disabled after switching themes.
- `pytest tests/ -m "not serial"`: 195 passed, 4 skipped.
- `pytest tests/ -m serial`: 1 passed.

## Notes

- On light-background terminals, dark-oriented themes may be hard to read — an inherent tradeoff of transparent TUIs.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #324 (stacked on that branch): extends the differential fuzzer's control-flow coverage with four new constructs that target the lowering paths where the previous session's merge/parallel-copy bugs lived. No new miscompiles surfaced — the #324 fixes hold under substantially harder control-flow stress, and this coverage now guards them permanently.

- **`Loop2`** — two loop-carried accumulators with parallel update semantics (both bodies see the old `(index, A, B)` frame, then both commit), so `bodyA = lb` / `bodyB = la` generates a genuine register swap on the back edge: the sharpest probe for parallel-copy sequencing and multi-argument block-invocation passing (asmjit #321 / BC-merge territory). `Node` gains a fourth kid slot and a `LoopAcc2` (`lb`) leaf; single-accumulator loops publish `acc2 == acc` so `lb` is legal in any loop body.
- **`LoopBreak`** — a real traced `if (...) break;` mid-body on a fixed accumulator predicate (ints: odd, floats: negative; NaN-safe), splitting the loop body's CFG — a shape no other loop kind produces.
- **`WhileLoop`** — compound data-dependent header condition (`i < trips && pred(acc)`), re-evaluated per iteration, exercising `val<bool>` conjunctions in loop headers.
- **`LoopIndexOuter`** (`lio`) — a doubly-nested body reads the *enclosing* loop's index, forcing outer-frame values to survive across the inner loop's back edge as extra block arguments.

All predicates are fixed and mirrored exactly between the native oracle (`EvalNative.hpp`) and the traced kernel (`EvalNautilus.hpp`), keeping every generated program fully defined by construction.

- Per-extension differential surveys (1500 / 2500 inputs), then a final sweep: **5000-input survey + 2000-input built-in corpus across interpreter + MLIR + C++ + BC + AsmJit — 0 findings** (macOS arm64).

Audit-confirmed correctness fix in `OrchestratorTaskService`.

## Bug (#3, high — 3/3 skeptics)
`reEngageOrEscalate` re-reads the task doc *specifically to preserve* an upstream metadata write from the same auto-verify pass (the completion envelope — see the comment). But it merged with `...doc?.task.metadata`: if the task was concurrently deleted (user cancels mid auto-verify), `doc` is null, the spread collapses to `{}`, and `updateTask` writes metadata back **without** the envelope. Guarded: if the re-read finds no task, bail (nothing to re-engage, nothing to preserve).

## Dispositions of the two sibling findings
- **`preserveHistory` "advertised but rejected"** — this is honest boundary validation, not larp: JSON callers can send `false`, and the boundary rejects destructive rerun with a clear `RecoveryConflictError` rather than silently ignoring intent. `boolean` is the correct type (tightening to `true` breaks the legitimate runtime `=== false` guard). Clarified with a doc comment; no behavior change.
- **`recordUsage` "orphaned foreign key"** — **false positive**. The store persists usage **inline in the task JSON document**; there is no usage table and no FK. Task-level usage without a live session row still totals correctly, and dropping it would lose accounting. No change.

## Evidence
```
$ bunx vitest run orchestrator-task-service → 59 passed
```

Refs #11028.

author: itkla
body:
Adds real outbound email. Before this, there was **no SMTP transport**: password-reset and email-change shipped with a seam whose only impl (`Logging*`) logged the link, and invites generated a token but never emailed it. This lands a Jakarta Mail engine and wires it in.

Closes #250. Follow-ups: #251 (email notification channel), #252 (React Email authoring workspace).

## What's included
- **Transport** (`spring-boot-starter-mail`): `MailProperties` (`connex.mail.*`), `MailService` (async, failure-tolerant), `JavaMailSenderFactory` (cached per config), `MailConfigResolver` (precedence), `EmailTemplateRenderer` (HTML templates, HTML-escaped tokens).
- **Secrets**: per-workspace SMTP password AES/GCM-encrypted at rest (`SecretCipher`, key from `CONNEX_MAIL_SECRET_KEY`); never returned to clients (write-only field, API exposes `hasPassword`/`configured` only); never logged.
- **Per-workspace config**: `workspace_mail_config` (V32), mapper, `WorkspaceMailConfigService` + `/api/workspaces/{id}/mail-config` (GET/PUT/DELETE + `POST /test`). Control-plane, `WORKSPACE_SETTINGS`-gated, excluded from the tenant-scope backstop like `AllowedDomainMapper`.
- **Wired seams**: real SMTP impls of `PasswordResetEmailService` + `EmailChangeEmailService` (`@Primary`, gated on `connex.mail.enabled`) supersede the logging fallbacks; token invites now emailed via the workspace sender.
- **Frontend**: Settings → Email page (`EmailPanel`) — host/port/from/credentials, TLS toggles, **Send test email**, remove; api client, types, en/ja i18n.
- **Styled templates**: inline-CSS, email-client-safe HTML (invite, password-reset, email-change, test).

## Config model & precedence
- **Instance default** via `CONNEX_MAIL_*` — used for account-level mail (reset, email-change) and as the fallback sender.
- **Per-workspace override** (Settings → Email) — used for workspace-scoped mail (invites). Precedence: enabled+usable workspace config → instance default → disabled (features degrade to today's logging fallback).
- Account-level mail always uses the instance sender (a user spans workspaces); never a tenant's SMTP.

## Verification
- **Backend verify loop** (fresh isolated schema + Mailpit, since removed): V32 applies; config CRUD with password **write-only + AES-encrypted at rest** (confirmed ciphertext in DB); **test email delivered** via workspace sender; **password-reset email delivered** via instance sender; **tenant isolation** — non-member gets **403** on GET/PUT/POST.
- **Tests**: `SecretCipher` round-trip/tamper/no-key, resolver precedence + `resolveWorkspaceOnly`, config-service RBAC + encryption + SSRF host guard. Full backend suite green (`./gradlew test`).
- **Frontend**: `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean on touched files.

## Adversarial review — addressed
- **SSRF (medium)**: workspace SMTP hosts resolving to private/loopback/link-local are **blocked** (`CONNEX_MAIL_ALLOW_INTERNAL_HOSTS` opt-out for on-prem relays); test-send returns a **generic** error (no port-scan oracle), detail logged server-side.
- **Test-send correctness**: now targets the workspace's **own** config only (no misleading instance-fallback success); resolves inside try (no 500 after key rotation).
- **UX**: `configured` flag makes Remove reachable for password-less configs; test button gates on saved (not draft) state; safe port parse.

## Notes / deferred
- ⚠️ **Flag precedence**: enabling `connex.mail.enabled` activates real reset/email-change mail regardless of the per-flow `*.email-enabled` flags (those still gate the logging fallbacks). Intended, but a deployer expecting `password-reset.email-enabled=false` to suppress reset mail should know.
- **Send-before-commit** (deferred): invite/reset mail dispatches inside the `@Transactional` method (async, cross-bean); a rollback after dispatch could email an invite that didn't persist. Matches the existing in-tx notification pattern; tracked for an `AFTER_COMMIT` refactor.
- **i18n**: templates render `en`; JP variants + a user-locale preference are part of #252.
- `CONNEX_MAIL_SECRET_KEY` is required once workspace passwords exist; rotating it invalidates stored passwords.
